messages:
deploy-bot: Finished rollout: ratecap-service v3 -> canary eu-central-1 at 2026-03-15T10:20Z. Canary=10% traffic. Release notes: token-accounting fixes + new exemption merge logic. CI: green. :rocket:
incidents-bot: Pager: ratecap-service 429 spike in eu-central-1 (10m window). Alerts: 429-ratecap, p99 latency increase. Link: https://internal/alerts/RCV3-429-euc1
maria_p: getting paged, will join. seeing 429s from embedding endpoints for some enterprise orgs.
kevin-oncall: I'm on it. handoff to oncall. starting quick triage. @suresh_eng @lisa-se fyi.
suresh_eng: logs show token_balance_delta negative for requests routed via dedicated-reserved path (dedicated-pool-id=gp-resv-7). That smells like a double-debit from the new accounting path.
lisa-se: customer support report: multiple premium customers seeing errors like "quota exceeded" even though they have reserved capacity. label: sev2. Customers: Acct-ENT-42, Acct-ENT-77, Acct-PLAT-9.
kevin-oncall: timeline: deploy at 10:20, alerts at 10:25. likely regression in exemption/route merge. mitigation options: 1) flip runtime feature flag kill-switch for ratecap_v3 2) apply targeted exemptions for affected accounts 3) rollback canary -> v2. Which is fastest?
maria_p: kill-switch flip should be fastest if flag is wired correctly. where's the flag? deploy-lead, confirm.
deploy-lead: flag path is config/ratecap/v3_enabled in our featureflag service. We have a kill-switch that can be flipped via the ops console or CLI. Verified earlier but... risk: flip affects global behavior. Prefer target exemptions first?
kevin-oncall: given customer impact (enterprise paid customers), plan: A) apply per-account exemptions for the three customers B) flip kill-switch if exemptions don't reduce 429s in 3 mins C) rollback canary if kill-switch not effective.
andy-infra: I can push exemptions now. command: ```./adminctl exemptions add --account Acct-ENT-42 --scope reserved_pool --reason "canary v3 token drift"``` will open bypass for that account. doing Acct-ENT-42, Acct-ENT-77, Acct-PLAT-9 simultaneously.
ops-bot: Exec started: adminctl exemptions add (3 accounts) by andy-infra at 2026-03-15T10:29:05Z.
kevin-oncall: applying exemptions now. monitor metrics: 429 rate and per-account success rate.
maria_p: after exemptions, Acct-ENT-42 200->500 reqs success increased to 92% (was 35%). still seeing throttles on mixed traffic where requests ride reserved path but don't get exempted.
suresh_eng: digging: the merge of exemption rules in v3 uses a short-circuit that accidentally drops exemptions that originate from legacy reserved-pool tags. Patch in code uses 'tag' vs 'pool_id' mismatch. reproducer in logs: ```if (!exemptions.contains(tag)) { // old code used pool_id }``` this leads to missing exemptions when matching route.
kevin-oncall: ok we have partial improvement but not universal. flip kill-switch in 2 mins if no full recovery. @deploy-lead authorize kill-switch?
deploy-lead: authorize. flip via CLI or console. prefer CLI so we have audit trail.
andy-infra: CLI command: ```ffctl set ratecap_v3_enabled false --actor kevin-oncall --reason "emergency: canary causing missing exemptions"``` Executing now.
ops-bot: Feature flag updated: ratecap_v3_enabled=false by kevin-oncall at 2026-03-15T10:34:12Z.
incidents-bot: Note: this flag flip triggered an automated telemetry check; canary traffic should route to v2 behavior within ~30s.
maria_p: within 45s I'm seeing 429s drop to baseline. p50/p95 latency back to normal. Enterprise customers report recovered.
lisa-se: support update: Evie, please send initial customer status: Acct-ENT-42/77/PLAT-9 recovered, other accounts may have transient errors.
evie-support: Sending customer messages now. Escalation note in CRM and support tickets created.
suresh_eng: root cause hypothesis: token-accounting path in v3 incorrectly reconciles tokens for requests that traverse the 'reserved' routing layer, causing double-debit and early exhaustion. Fix: align tag matching and expand unit tests for reserved_pool path.
kevin-oncall: mitigation timeline: exemptions applied 10:29 -> partial recovery; flag flip 10:34 -> full recovery 10:35. will not roll back canary further since flag flip reverted runtime behavior quickly.
deploy-lead: rolling back the canary is low value now but we should still push a hotfix to v3 and re-run a constrained canary after tests.
maria_p: impact estimate: ~18% of eu-central reserved-pool traffic hit 429s during window (10:25-10:34). Affected enterprise requests ~3.2k failed requests total, 5 known high-touch customers saw degraded UX. No data leakage.
lisa-se: severity classified as sev2; customer SLA impacts for a handful of enterprise customers; support to follow up with crediting if needed.
andy-infra: created a debug snapshot & logs: https://internal/logs/snapshots/2620001234. Retention note: keep 30d for incident.
suresh_eng: quick patch in PR: fix tag->pool_id matching + add unit test + e2e covering exemptions. PR: https://git/repo/pulls/4871. request: expedite review.
kevin-oncall: handoff: @andy-infra and @suresh_eng are taking L2 follow-ups. I'll update oncall rotation that we contained via flag and exemptions. Oncall timeline saved to incident-runbook.
incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03215-001. Severity: sev2. Affected region: eu-central-1. Lead: kevin-oncall. Postmortem owner: suresh_eng. Link: https://internal/incidents/INC-2026-03215-001
maria_p: tagging follow-ups: - ship patch and run small canary - add unit/e2e tests for reserved route - add observability for exemption-matching failures - add playbook step to flip kill-switch for new feature flags
evie-support: opened customer cases for affected customers and templated comms for follow-up.
deploy-bot: Canary state: paused. v3 feature flag false. Awaiting hotfix merge & canary smoke tests.
kevin-oncall: closing pager. leave thread open for postmortem notes. thanks team. :heart:
